Captain of Reserve Op Team A6, Rhodes Island HR Office Person of the Year, and founder of the onboard fashion magazine 'Orchid'. At her own request, she has now been reclassified as a Sniper Operator. While retaining her battlefield support capabilities, she has also made significant progress in offensive ability. In addition, she frequently offers constructive suggestions of her own accord while carrying out various missions.

Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 8%
Operator Orchid's surface crystals have increased significantly compared with several years ago.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Orchid currently shows no signs of acute lesions, and her other physical indicators are within normal ranges for her current stage.

The magazine 'Orchid' is now practically known to everyone aboard Rhodes Island. Personally overseen by Ms. Orchid and named after her own operator codename, this fashion magazine is astonishing for both the richness of its content and the professionalism of its perspective. Today, we have the honor of interviewing the magazine's founder, Ms. Orchid.
Interviewer: Ms. Orchid, may I ask what led you to found this magazine?
Orchid: Ever since joining Rhodes Island, one of the things I've always done is help the Infected conceal the crystals on their bodies through fashion and trends. The operators and patients who came to me for that... There were honestly a lot of them. All I can say is, we're all people, and everyone has the right to pursue fashion. I think that's a wonderful thing. But there really were a few too many people coming to me, so I started thinking that instead of having them come one by one, I might as well teach everyone some methods all at once.
Interviewer: So you founded this magazine?
Orchid: No. To be honest, work in HR is already busy enough to kill me. Although the thought had crossed my mind, I never seriously considered actually making it happen.
Interviewer: Huh? Then—
Orchid: There was a time when Catapult and Spot thought I was too much of a nag, so they wanted to find something for me to do. They went behind my back and applied to produce the magazine, even putting together a decent-looking sample issue and giving it to me on my birthday. I was actually really moved at the time, which feels so stupid now that I think about it. But since they had already made it, I felt it was a rare opportunity, so I took over and kept it going.
Interviewer: Then the names listed on the staff list—
Graphic Design: Spot
Editing and Proofreading: Midnight
Models: Spot, Midnight, Popukar, Catapult...
Contributing Writer: Catapult
Could it be—
Orchid: Hah. They made up their minds that I would take over. Did they really think they could get away with it?
Interviewer: I-I see. However, there are a great many magazines, training classes, and hobby groups founded aboard the ship by operators based on their personal interests, but most of them are affected in terms of content production and activity frequency by how busy the operators are with missions and how long they remain aboard the ship. Yet 'Orchid,' as a monthly magazine, has not skipped a single issue since its founding. In other words, while the beginning may not have been ideal, the process and the results have been good, right?
Orchid: What do you think, Spot?
Spot: Kill me. Please don't make me draw layouts anymore. I just want to read comics.
Orchid: Midnight?
Midnight: Have mercy on me, Ms. Orchid. I've seen the word 'clothing' so much I'm about to completely fall apart.
Orchid: Catapult?
Catapult: I never wrote this much even when I was in school!
Orchid: What about you, Popukar?
Popukar: I like being Orchid's model!
Orchid: Spot has trained his drawing skills, Midnight has less free time to harass others, Catapult has time to study, Popukar has new clothes to wear, and I get to do something I've always been interested in. It really is quite nice, isn't it?
Interviewer: ...Ahaha, let's talk about how you gather material!

After completing the report on her strange journey, Orchid secretly submitted an application, hoping to learn why Dr. Kal'tsit brought Popukar back to Rhodes Island in the first place.
After learning the full picture of the Houei incident, the Doctor and Amiya also believed this was necessary. In the past, everyone only knew that Popukar's eye was special. However, having a special eye is not all that uncommon on Rhodes Island. It is just that Orchid's experiences seem to prove that Popukar's eye, as well as her background, are far from that simple.
This was not because Orchid did not trust Rhodes Island or Dr. Kal'tsit. Quite the opposite, in fact. After all, it would be absolutely impossible for Dr. Kal'tsit not to know about Popukar's background. Then why had she hidden it? This became a question that lingered in Orchid's mind.
At the meeting held for this purpose, Dr. Kal'tsit first apologized to Orchid, as what Orchid and Catapult had experienced had exceeded her expectations. As a result, she could not yet clearly explain the connection between Popukar and Hofukaru to Orchid, and needed time to clarify the specifics.
However, when it came to what Orchid was truly worried about, Dr. Kal'tsit gave a clear answer. From the very beginning, Dr. Kal'tsit had no intention in assigning Popukar to Team A6 beyond hoping Orchid would take care of her, and now, there could not possibly be any other environment where Popukar would feel more at ease. For the sake of Popukar's mental stability, Dr. Kal'tsit also hopes Team A6 can become more closely connected.
'Popukar is simply a good child growing up strong and healthy at Rhodes Island, and that will never change.'
Orchid accepted this answer.
When all is said and done, she does not care what secret is buried within Popukar. Perhaps it is important, but to her, it is not that important. Just like what she hopes for herself and everyone around her, she only wants Popukar to live happily.
After the meeting ended, she had already made up her mind—she had already told the others in A6 once about her experiences in Houei, but she intended to tell them again. This time, she would be sure to focus on the far too flighty blacksmith, the far too serious general, and the far too strong princess.

Orchid has a very good relationship with her family.
In that regard, she could be considered something of an outlier in A6. After all, Popukar was taken in by Dr. Kal'tsit, Midnight has almost cut off contact with his family, much like Spot, and as for Catapult, being an orphan, she does not even know her parents' names.
The other members of A6 do not avoid discussing matters related to Orchid's family. They all know that Orchid's parents care greatly about their daughter's health, and did not distance themselves from her after she contracted Oripathy. Orchid, in turn, writes to her parents regularly to keep them informed of how she is doing. The members of A6 all consider this a good thing.
Orchid admits she has been fortunate in this regard. Her parents have never restricted her choices regarding her work or her future, and after she accidentally contracted Oripathy, they supported her decision to go to Rhodes Island. They have always told her that she can come home whenever she wants, and that they are willing to give up many things for her.
Her parents are always concerned for her, always asking if she intends to come back. This is only natural. In the eyes of many, no matter how famous a pharmaceutical company Rhodes Island may be, as long as the Infected are involved, the future will always remain uncertain. To Orchid's family, living aboard Rhodes Island is ultimately not the best choice—
'...Your mother and I have talked it over. We can sell our house and move somewhere more remote to live together. Your mother and I can take care of you, and you won't have to worry about anything... We believe Rhodes Island is a good company, but what could be happier than having family together again?'
Her father once wrote this in a letter, and at that time, she found herself unable to give a reply.
How was she supposed to answer? Tell her parents that her work here was going fairly smoothly, and that she had made a group of friends who, while strange in personality, were decent people?
So what? That did not seem to conflict with going home. No job could last a lifetime, and no friends would stay together forever, but family was different. Family was connected by blood. Besides, her family loved her so much, and she loved her parents too.
She had no grand ambitions. She thought Rhodes Island's ideals were great, and she was willing to do what she could for the Infected. Or rather, by the time she realized it, she had already devoted years of her life to this cause. She had also come to understand how the Elite Operators thought, but she felt she could not be like them.
Perhaps things could simply remain as they were. Once her condition worsened a little more and she could no longer work, or for some other reason, she would leave this place, return to her parents, and quietly wait for death to come.
For someone Infected, this was already a happy enough life.
She had imagined this before, but she still could not bring herself to put pen to paper and reply to her parents. Something was holding her back, and she could not say what it was, so she always gave vague answers and avoided the subject.
And this was not the first time.

Back when she had yet to contract Oripathy and was still working as a magazine editor, her parents would ask her if that was her ideal job. She never gave them an answer.
She liked fashion, and she liked tailoring, but whether she should make that profession her life's pursuit? She felt she could not say for certain. She could not simply stop thinking about the choices before her, and so she always thought far too much. To others, this made her seem like she was always prepared for the future, but only she knew she had simply been fortunate enough to have the right to choose in certain matters.
A choice that would decide one's entire life was far too difficult to make. After all, a person's life was simply too long—that was what she used to think, but she could not bring herself to tell her parents not to discuss the matter for that reason. Later, her parents even stopped bringing up such discussions in their letters, because they knew it would leave her conflicted. In the end, she knew that this was an ultimate question she herself wanted to answer—
What exactly do I want to do with my life?
And before she could find an answer, she contracted Oripathy. She came to Rhodes Island for treatment, became an Operator, took on the role of A6's captain, and in the blink of an eye, several years had passed.
As for the answer to that ultimate question, she still had no clue whatsoever. Not only that, but the pain brought by Oripathy reminded her at every moment that her life was no longer as long as she had once imagined.
This is just hopeless. After returning from Sargon, she thought this as she faced yet another letter from home.
Even more despairing was the fact that she realized that now, whenever she thought, 'a person's life is too long,' she would already add on in Spot's tone—'Well, at least now that I've got Oripathy, it isn't quite so long anymore.'
Forget making any progress. She feels like she has already been assimilated by these people... Under Popukar's surprised gaze, she slumped down onto the desk in defeat.
Thinking about it carefully, it really did seem like she had not made the slightest progress over these past few years.
She thought of Penny and Jerry, and of the wedding dress that still appeared in her dreams to this day. She had replayed that night in her mind countless times, and still could not think of a better way she could have handled it.
She thought of what Catapult had said at the end of the Zinogre hunt. Yes, she was always telling the people around her that life ought to have an answer, but the truth was, she herself had no answer when it came to that.
She was always like this, saying one thing while thinking another, always demanding things of others that she herself might not even be able to do.
Sometimes, she really did hate that about herself.
Even after all the effort it took to make that trip through Houei, in the end, apart from this set of equipment and a few memories, the only thing that could be called a gain was that she had become a little more honest with herself.
But when she turned her attention back to how she should reply to her parents' letter, she was somewhat surprised to find that, this time, in addition to the usual updates on how she had been and asking after their health, there was something else she wanted to write.
'...I've introduced my teammates to you many times, but you have never really had the chance to meet and talk with them. Lately, I've been thinking that perhaps the next time I go to Columbia on a field assignment, I could bring them to meet you.'
She wrote those words almost as if it were only natural.
Of course, that was not an answer.
It was just that, sometimes, being a little more honest with yourself meant letting go of certain fixations. Perhaps there were some jobs one could do for a lifetime, perhaps there were some friends one could spend a lifetime with, and perhaps these things did not conflict with one another.
She decided to give it a try.

Orchid has been showing up at the training grounds far more often than she used to.
This has not drawn as much attention as Catapult's change, as Orchid has always been the type to diligently complete her training. In others' eyes, she has simply become a little more proactive than before.
However, Dobermann, as her instructor, has still noticed some subtle changes.
In the past, Orchid only completed training to meet the requirements expected of an Operator. Beyond that, she felt no need to improve her own combat abilities. But after returning from Sargon, changing her equipment, and even altering her tactical position, Orchid has indeed undergone some changes in this regard.
Yet Dobermann also knows that this cannot be so simply summarized as Orchid wanting to get stronger, or Orchid developing her own ideas about combat. Anyone who stands beside Orchid and watches the state she is in while training would understand that much.
It is more like she is searching for something in combat.
Before one training session, Dobermann spoke with Orchid about this.
'...Stance, nock, aim, draw, release. The steps to archery are as simple and easy to understand as designing clothes.' Faced with Dobermann, an instructor and friend she had known for years, Orchid thought the question over carefully.
'So you think it has something in common with your hobby?'
'No.' Orchid shook her head. 'Designing clothes requires thinking about many things. It requires creativity. But archery... For me, the important part may be that when I shoot, all I have to do is aim at the target. I do not have to think about anything else.'
Orchid paused, seeming to spend some effort before finally saying what came next. 'I can control it. Yes, I suppose I should say that it is something I can fully control.'
'Control?' Dobermann was somewhat surprised to hear that word from Orchid.
'Yes. I once heard that by doing small things like folding clothes or cleaning, people can gradually build up a sense of control over their lives, and ultimately gain the confidence to face life. I never used to believe that, but...' As Orchid spoke, she lifted the bow in her hand. Stance, nock, aim, draw, release. The arrow struck the center of the target. 'When I am practicing archery, I do feel as if I can control myself a little better.'
'What surprises me is that even you need to use this method to control yourself.'
'To be honest, even I am surprised.' Orchid smiled with a touch of resignation. 'But how should I put it? I was never the kind of person who felt confident about everything, and I do not know if this feeling is truly useful. It is just that now, whenever I feel upset, I want to come practice archery.'
With that, Orchid picked up her bow and arrows and walked toward the training grounds. Watching Orchid like this, Dobermann was both happy that she had found a new interest, and surprised by her lack of self-awareness in one certain respect.
'Does she realize that simply taking her stance, nocking, aiming, drawing, and releasing, and then hitting the target, is not something just anyone can do?'
